name: action-button
description: Press the iPhone or iPad Action Button once. The press is dispatched without activating the session app and nothing is re-observed afterwards, so the app keeps the state the press found. What the system does with the press is not observed by this command: Simulators run no Shortcuts or App Intents, so delivery to an assigned Shortcut is verifiable only on a physical iPhone. Times out after 90s.

name: alert
description: Inspect, wait for, accept, or dismiss a platform alert. Use get before acting when the alert content matters; accept and dismiss change the active alert state. Each iOS XCTest execution activates once, then only observes. Local Apple XCTest and Limrun iOS choose recognized English labels by preference (Allow While Using App before Allow Once); equal-ranked choices and unknown labels refuse, including a lone unknown button. Open, Done, and Confirm… accept; Keep Browsing, Deny, and Skip dismiss. On the Apple XCUITest runner, dismiss taps only a recognized decline label (Cancel, Don't Allow, Ask App Not to Track, and similar) or the close element of a popover whose accessibility marker reads exactly "dismiss popup"; when no button fits the action, accept and dismiss answer ALERT_BUTTON_NOT_FOUND having tapped nothing — read labels with alert get, then press the button by label. Inspect again after an unconfirmed action; never assume a timeout means nothing happened. Times out after 90s.

name: app-switcher
description: Open the device app switcher to inspect or change foreground apps. This changes the visible system UI and may move focus away from the current app. Times out after 90s.

name: apps
description: List the apps installed on the selected device. Include system or OEM apps only when they are needed as automation targets. Times out after 90s.

A capture failure reports an unknown outcome. Times out after 90s; a caller-supplied budget extends it.

name: click

A ref or selector target is re-checked for motion before dispatch when the session's previous action just animated the screen, and is dispatched at its resting position; one that has not stopped refuses with target_still_moving rather than acting where it was. Times out after 90s; a caller-supplied budget extends it.

description: Read the current device clipboard text, or replace its contents with the given text. Times out after 90s.

name: close

Android ADB close fails with android-app-close-timeout if the app stays foreground, or its process stays running, past its 2s check window. Times out after 90s.

name: debug

Times out after 90s.

name: find
description: Find by text/label/value/role/id and run action. The role locator matches snapshot kind vocabulary (button, text, text-field, switch, ...); pre-reconciliation leaf spellings (statictext, edittext, textview) stay accepted on the nodes that carried them during a deprecation window. Times out after 90s.

record.description: Force-record this out-of-band observation into a repair-armed heal (mutually exclusive with noRecord). Authored replay steps are recorded automatically and never need this. On find, valid only for a read-only action.

name: focus
description: Move input focus to explicit screen coordinates without entering text. Prefer semantic interactions when a snapshot ref or selector is available; use type or fill after focus. Times out after 90s.

name: fold
description: Fold or unfold a foldable iPhone simulator (iPhone Duo) or a foldable Android emulator into the closed, half-open, or open pose. iOS sends a simulator HID hinge event, then reads the hinge angle back inside the simulator to confirm it, and can follow timestamped angle keyframes; Android sets the emulator console posture, then confirms the device state the guest commits and reports the hinge angle the AVD profile defines for that posture, and dismisses the lock screen a fold to the cover display can raise. On iOS a pose change moves the app to a different panel with a different point size; on Android a fold to or from closed moves the app between the cover and inner displays, and any pose change can reshape the app window, whose size the next snapshot reports. Either way every ref and coordinate from before it is stale: re-snapshot after this command. Taps, long presses, and scrolling target the app window on its current panel in closed, half-open, and open poses. Simulator and emulator only; iOS requires the iOS simulator SDK; Device Hub and host Accessibility permission are not required. An iOS simulator in a scoped simulator set folds the same way as one in the default set. Times out after 255s.

pose.description: Instant preset; mutually exclusive with keyframes.

keyframes.description: Piecewise-linear hinge motion. Start at 0ms; strictly increasing timestamps, up to 60000ms. Repeated angles create holds. Mutually exclusive with pose.

name: gesture
description: Perform a structured pan, fling, swipe, pinch, rotate, transform, tap, or drag gesture. Select the gesture kind, then provide only the inputs that apply to that kind. A tap touches 2 to 5 points at once; repeat it with count and pauseMs. Times out after 90s.

delta.description: Movement delta for pan or transform gestures.

points.description: Tap contact points, held together for holdMs.

count.description: Tap repetitions; the same contacts run this many times.

pauseMs.description: Delay between tap repetitions, added to each repetition’s own time.

destinationHoldMs.description: Hold before releasing at the destination.

name: get
description: Read text or accessibility attributes from a snapshot ref or selector without changing the app. Use format text for visible content or attrs for the element attribute map. Times out after 90s.

name: hardware-button
description: Press a phone hardware button once: volume-up, volume-down, power, mute, sleep, wake, media-play-pause, media-next, media-previous, media-rewind, or media-fast-forward. The press is dispatched without activating the session app and nothing is re-observed afterwards, so the OS decides what the key does — which audio stream a volume press moves, which media session a media key reaches, and whether the HUD shows, is device behavior this command does not claim. Power toggles the Android screen; sleep and wake are the explicit Android events that turn it off or on without toggling, and after a press that turns it off, later commands may hit a locked screen. Android (ADB-backed and Appium) presses all eleven on phones and tablets; a physical iPhone or iPad presses volume only through the local runner or Appium, never power, mute, sleep, wake, or media. iOS Simulators, Android TV and tvOS targets refuse: on TV targets use tv-remote. Times out after 90s.

button.description: One press each. volume-up and volume-down move the system volume stream the OS selects; power toggles the screen on Android; sleep and wake are the explicit Android events that turn the screen off or on without toggling; mute, media-play-pause, media-next, media-previous, media-rewind, and media-fast-forward are Android keys the OS routes to its own streams and media sessions. All of these except volume are refused on every Apple leaf.

A device that never frees, or is taken again while this open waits, costs the full budget, which extends this command's timeout envelope rather than eating into it.

name: scroll
description: Scroll in a direction, or toward the top/bottom edge of scrollable content. Set until to a selector to reach an off-screen target in one command rather than a scroll-and-check loop. The optional amount is the finger-path fraction of the viewport axis, honored up to 0.8 of it; directional scrolls reduce release momentum, while app scroll physics determine the final content offset. A visible keyboard shortens the swiped band instead of being dismissed; when too little is left, the command refuses with scroll_keyboard_occludes_surface. A directional scroll also reports the movement it observed as movement: moved, at-edge, unchanged, or unobserved when the two reads could not back a claim either way; an unchanged surface inside a container that still hides content in that direction refuses with scroll_no_progress rather than repeating the requested distance. The movement field is absent where a tier verifies per pass (top/bottom, until), where the runtime cannot read a screen, or where a settle observation or a replay already owns that observation. Times out after 90s; a caller-supplied budget extends it.

until.description: Repeat scroll passes until this selector is visible on screen, then stop. Not valid with the top/bottom edge directions, which carry their own stop condition.

maxPasses.description: Maximum scroll gestures for an until search (default 12). Requires until.

durationMs.description: Scroll duration in milliseconds when the backend supports pacing.

force.description: Atomically replace an existing save-script target.

name: settings
description: Read or change supported operating-system settings, animation scales, appearance, or app permissions on the selected target. Platform support varies by setting and action. Times out after 90s.

app.description: App the change targets, by bundle id, package name, or app name: the app `clear-app-state` clears, or the app a `permission` change (or an iOS-simulator `location on|off` privacy change) lands on. A name resolves to the installed app as `open` resolves it: an iOS simulator matches display names and accepts only an installed bundle id, Android accepts only an installed package and refuses a name that resolves to an intent with `setting_app_not_package`, and a Limrun iOS session resolves only the `settings` alias. One that resolves to nothing is refused with `app_not_installed` before anything changes. The app need not be running. Without it the session app is used; a device-wide change (`location set` on any target, the Android `location on|off` toggle, `mobile-data`, macOS permissions) refuses one with `setting_app_not_consumed`. The CLI reads it only from this invocation, never from `AGENT_DEVICE_TARGET_APP` or config `targetApp`.

The names are for PLANNING, not invocation: there is no API to trigger them, so reach the affordance through the element detail screen, through the same control exposed as a labeled element elsewhere, or by coordinates from its rect. iOS simulator only; costs one accessibility round trip per merged element.

The call screen or notification can cover the app, so re-snapshot afterwards. Times out after 90s.

action.description: call starts an incoming call, accept answers it, cancel ends it, sms delivers a text message.

number.description: Caller or sender phone number: digits with an optional leading +.

text.description: Message text for sms; required for sms and refused for the call actions. The emulator drops characters outside the Basic Multilingual Plane, such as emoji.

name: test
description: Run one or more replay scripts as a serial test suite Streams progress; no fixed client timeout.

platform.description: Platform selector used to resolve a device.

device.description: Device name selector (a UDID belongs in udid, a serial in serial).

udid.description: Apple device or simulator UDID; the selector that pins one device when several share a name.

serial.description: Android, HarmonyOS, or Vega VVD serial selector.

metroHost.description: Metro/debug host hint inherited by each test session.

metroPort.description: Metro/debug port hint inherited by each test session.

bundleUrl.description: Bundle URL hint inherited by each test session.

testIme.description: Activate the headless Android test IME for the sessions each suite attempt opens (default on for emulators; opt-in on real devices).

name: trace
description: Start or stop trace-log capture and return the resulting artifact when capture ends. Without a path, start writes a timestamped trace log named after the session in the sessions directory of the daemon state; a path on stop moves the finished trace there. Times out after 90s.

name: trigger-app-event
description: Ask the app to handle an app-defined automation or test event, with an optional structured payload. Call this only for event names and payload shapes the app documents. Times out after 90s.

event.description: Name of an app-defined automation or test event the app documents.

payload.description: Structured payload passed to the event, in the shape the app documents for it.

name: type
description: Append text to the currently focused input. Use fill when the existing field value should be replaced, and focus first when no input is active. Times out after 90s.

name: uninstall
description: Remove an installed app from the selected device. A package name or bundle id that is not installed succeeds with wasInstalled: false. Times out after 180s.

platform.description: Platform selector used to resolve a device.

device.description: Device name selector (a UDID belongs in udid, a serial in serial).

udid.description: Apple device or simulator UDID; the selector that pins one device when several share a name.

serial.description: Android, HarmonyOS, or Vega VVD serial selector.

app.description: Package name, bundle id, or installed app name.

name: wait
description: Wait for a duration, text, snapshot ref, selector to appear, selector to be strictly absent, or stable UI. Use the strict absence target when zero selector matches are required; stable waits until the UI stays quiet for the requested window. Times out after 90s; a caller-supplied budget extends it.

name: help
description: Usage guides. No topic: the root decision card. topic = one of commands, manual-qa, maestro, workflow, scripting, gestures, tv, debugging, react-devtools, cdp, react-native, physical-device, ios-system-ui, foldable, remote, macos, web, dogfood, validate for that guide, or a tool name for its complete flag reference. For specialized work or an unclear command shape only; not a startup step, not needed after an error that carries a hint.

topic.description: Guide topic or tool name; omit for the card.
